subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on programming concepts, then mark my answer against the CCEA spec.
promptWeak: Explain programming concepts for GCSE CCEA Computer Science simply, with an example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: What is the difference between a variable and a constant?
options: A constant can change value; a variable cannot
Both can change at any time
A variable can change value while the program runs; a constant keeps the same value throughout
questions.explain: A variable is a named store whose value can change during execution. A constant is given a value once and that value cannot change while the program runs.

questions.q: A program uses the value of Pi (3.14159) many times but it should never change. It is best stored as a:
questions.explain: Because the value must never change, Pi should be a constant. This also makes the code clearer and prevents accidental changes.

questions.q: Which data type would best store the value True or False?
questions.explain: A Boolean data type stores one of two values: True or False. It is ideal for yes/no or on/off conditions.

questions.q: A price of 19.99 should be stored using which data type?
questions.explain: A real (floating-point) number can store values with a fractional part, such as 19.99. An integer can only store whole numbers.

questions.q: Which data type stores a single letter or symbol such as 'A' or '?'
questions.explain: A character stores a single symbol. A string, by contrast, stores a sequence of characters such as a word or sentence.

questions.q: What does the programming construct 'sequence' mean?
options: Carrying out instructions one after another in a set order
Storing many values under one name
questions.explain: Sequence means the instructions are executed one after another in the exact order they are written.

questions.q: Which construct lets a program choose between different actions depending on a condition?
questions.explain: Selection uses statements such as IF...THEN...ELSE or SELECT CASE to run different code depending on whether a condition is true or false.

questions.q: IF score >= 50 THEN OUTPUT 'Pass' ELSE OUTPUT 'Fail'. If score is 50, what is output?
questions.explain: >= means 'greater than or equal to'. Since 50 is equal to 50, the condition is true and 'Pass' is output.

questions.q: What is iteration in programming?
questions.explain: Iteration means repeating a block of code. Loop types include FOR (count-controlled), WHILE and REPEAT (condition-controlled).

questions.q: Which loop is most suitable when you do NOT know in advance how many times it must repeat?
questions.explain: A WHILE loop (condition-controlled) is best when the number of repetitions is unknown, because it keeps repeating until its condition becomes false.

questions.q: FOR i = 1 TO 4: OUTPUT i. How many numbers are printed?
questions.explain: The loop runs for i = 1, 2, 3, 4, printing four numbers in total.

questions.q: In many languages, what does 17 MOD 5 give?
questions.explain: MOD gives the remainder after division. 17 divided by 5 is 3 remainder 2, so 17 MOD 5 = 2.

questions.q: Using integer (whole-number) division, what is 17 DIV 5?
questions.explain: DIV performs integer division, giving only the whole-number part of the result. 17 divided by 5 is 3 (remainder ignored).

questions.q: Which operator means 'not equal to' in typical pseudocode?
questions.explain: The operator <> means 'not equal to'. (A single = is used for assignment or equality depending on the language.)

questions.q: A program line reads: age = INPUT('Enter your age'). What does this do?
options: Waits for the user to type a value and stores it in the variable age
Compares age to a stored value
questions.explain: An INPUT statement pauses the program, lets the user type a value, and stores that value in the named variable (here, age).

questions.q: What is a key benefit of using subroutines (procedures/functions)?
options: They make the program run without any variables
They remove the need for loops
They break a program into reusable named blocks, making it easier to write and maintain
questions.explain: Subroutines split a program into smaller named blocks that can be reused and tested separately, reducing repetition and making code easier to maintain.

questions.q: What is the main difference between a function and a procedure?
options: A function cannot take any inputs
A procedure always returns a value; a function never does
A function returns a value to the code that called it; a procedure does not have to
questions.explain: A function returns a value to the part of the program that called it. A procedure carries out a task but does not have to return a value.

questions.q: What is an array?
options: A data structure that stores many values of the same type under one name, accessed by index
A single variable that holds one value
questions.explain: An array stores a collection of values of the same data type under one identifier. Each element is accessed using an index (position number).

questions.q: An array names = ['Amy','Ben','Cara','Dan'] uses index numbering starting at 0. What is names[2]?
questions.explain: With zero-based indexing, index 0 is 'Amy', 1 is 'Ben', 2 is 'Cara'. So names[2] is 'Cara'.

questions.q: Why is an array better than using separate variables for storing 100 exam marks?
options: Arrays cannot be used with loops
One array with a loop can store and process all 100 marks, instead of 100 named variables
Arrays run faster than the processor
questions.explain: An array lets you store many related values under one name and process them efficiently with a loop, rather than declaring and handling 100 individual variables.
